productPageReviews.reviewDescription: There's 31 pages to color in here, 4 are of a witch stirring a caldron (although one is a skeleton), 4 are of a scarecrow with a pumpkin head, and 3 are of a witch flying on a broom. It feels like coloring the same pages over and over. Other than that it was an alright coloring book, lots of halloween themed pictures. Not sure what makes it vintage or retro, though.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on June 26, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: It states that the drawings are from the 1920s and 1930s but I remember them from my childhood in the 1970s. Truly so much fun coloring them. I will say I did take the book to work and make a few copies of my favorite pictures. lol. If you have a soft spot for 'vintage' Halloween, you will love this book.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I love everything Halloween. I also love to color with my kids so this is the perfect coloring book for me. My kids even like it with the simple pictures and bold lines.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I love Halloween, so I really wanted to love this coloring book too! More than half of the book has decent vintage Halloween images. But then suddenly things take a turn with scenes repeating from different angles and what appears to be AI slop.Examples: AI weirdness starts with an image of a cat/witch/bat combined in one. Continues with a witch with no legs standing by a cauldron, a single ghost with bird wings, a cat behind a pumpkin but somehow it's front legs are in front of the pumpkin standing on nothing in particular, and a grim reaper with no legs standing by a jack-o'-lantern.I'm giving it 3 stars based on what wasn't ruined by AI.

aPlusContent.title: From the Publisher
aPlusContent.rawText:
From the Publisher
Time-Tested Tools 
Our learning materials have helped educate three generations of kids, creating life-long learners, and the legacy continues. Digital content, flash cards, workbooks, readers, toys and games—all are crafted through a child’s eyes, while integrating parent and teacher standards. 
Writing by Hand Improves Memory 
Writing in workbook pages, as opposed to typing on a computer, can help kids focus and learn. Writing by hand fires up specific areas of a child's brain, improving the ability to both remember what he or she learns and to think of new ideas. 
Longer Retention 
Kids and parents who use our flash cards for practice testing are using one of the most effective learning techniques available. A hundred years of research shows practice testing is highly likely to boost retention. 
Reading Has Lifelong Benefits 
A love of reading has been proven to have far-reaching benefits for children, emotionally and academically. And children who enjoy reading become confident readers and read more often. 
Kids Love Technology 
School Zone’s digital content supports children’s learning goals by enhancing problem-solving and critical thinking, as well as reinforcing skills through multisensory activities. It also improves language skills, increases motivation to stay on task, and stimulates curiosity and imagination. 
Not Just for Fun 
When kids play games together, they learn a healthy sense of competition and experience the joy of winning and empathy for losing. Along the way, they learn collaboration, cooperation, and problem-solving. Creative play stimulates imagination and nurtures emotional well-being.
